research_issues.question: In Atlanta, Georgia, what laws govern recreational marijuana and medical cannabis, including possession, use, and any city-level rules?
What federal cannabis restrictions remain relevant to marijuana use or possession in Atlanta?

propositions.claim: Recreational marijuana is not generally legal in Atlanta: Georgia’s Department of Public Health says marijuana is not legal in Georgia and that possession by an unauthorized person violates state law. Atlanta’s October 11, 2017 announcement described a city ordinance setting a maximum $75 fine and no jail time for possession of one ounce or less under the City Code, but expressly said the ordinance did not legalize possession or displace state law. That announcement is historical and does not establish whether the city rule has since been amended.

Georgia provides a limited medical-cannabis exception: eligible patients and caregivers with an active Medical Cannabis card may possess up to 12,000 milligrams of THC or medical cannabis. The state says physician certification is required and that this exception does not legalize all forms of marijuana. The Department of Public Health page was updated July 1, 2026.

Federal law separately prohibits knowingly possessing a controlled substance unless it was obtained through a valid prescription or order, or possession is otherwise authorized by federal law. DEA reports a final rule placing FDA-approved marijuana products and state-licensed medical-marijuana products in Schedule III, while broader marijuana rescheduling remains in a separate rulemaking process; therefore, Georgia’s medical-cannabis authorization should not be treated as a blanket statement about federal legality for every cannabis product or use.

research_issues.question: Under California law, how long does a residential landlord have to return a tenant’s security deposit after the tenancy ends?

propositions.claim: Under California law, a residential landlord generally has 21 days after the tenant moves out to return the full security deposit, or to provide an itemized statement of deductions and refund any balance. If cleaning or repair work cannot reasonably be completed within that period, the landlord may provide a good-faith estimate and must send the receipts within 14 days after the work is completed.

research_issues.question: En California, ¿cuánto tiempo tiene el arrendador de una vivienda para devolver el depósito de seguridad y qué reglas aplican a las deducciones?

propositions.claim: En California, después de que el inquilino desocupa la vivienda, el arrendador tiene 21 días para devolver todo el depósito o devolver el saldo y entregar un estado detallado de las deducciones, indicando qué se descontó y por qué.

Las deducciones permitidas incluyen, en general, renta impaga; limpieza necesaria para dejar la vivienda tan limpia como estaba al inicio; y reparación de daños causados por el inquilino o sus invitados, excluido el desgaste normal. Para deducciones superiores a $125, la guía de los tribunales indica que deben adjuntarse facturas o recibos; si el arrendador o su empleado hizo el trabajo, debe describirse el trabajo, el tiempo empleado y la tarifa por hora, que debe ser razonable.

Si por una razón válida la limpieza o reparación no se termina dentro de los 21 días, el arrendador puede enviar una estimación razonable y de buena fe del costo; debe entregar los recibos dentro de los 14 días posteriores a la terminación del trabajo.
